source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: Elucidatio capituli primi: Verbum Domini quod factum est ad Michæam.
1.title_en: Explanation of the first chapter: The word of the Lord that came to Micheas.

paras.t: Michæas sanctus Dei propheta, cujus liber mysteriis et pulchritudine sensuum plenus est, sextus est in ordine duodecim Prophetarum. Qui libro suo prologum brevem præmittens, tempus suæ vaticinationis ostendit, dicendo : Verbum Domini quod factum est ad Michæam Morasthiten, id est, sermo prophetalis a Deo per angelum dictus Michæ, oriundo de Morasthi viculo parvo, apud urbem Palæstinæ Eleutheropolim sito, in diebus Joathan, Achaz et Ezechiæ regum Juda. Non ponit nomina regum Israel seu decem tribuum sub quibus prophetavit, quia expressis regibus Juda quibus in regnando contemporanei erant, faciliter intelliguntur. Superius quoque dictum est, quod Osee et Amos, imo et Isaias sub Ozia, Joathan, Achaz et Ezechia, prophetarunt. Hic autem Michæas non legitur prophetasse sub Ozia patre Joathan. Ex quo elicitur, quod Michæas cœpit sub Joathan vaticinari : et pro parte prophetavit eodem tempore quo Osee, Isaias et Amos, quamvis post illos incepit. Ex his insuper constat, quod iste Michæas sit alter ab illo de quo tertio Regum habetur, qui sub Achab prophetavit, de quo Achab dixit ad Josaphat : Ego odi eum, quia non prophetat mihi nisi malum. Ille itaque diu præcessit istum Michæam : et dictus fuit Michæas filius Jemla.
paras.en: Micheas, the holy prophet of God, whose book is full of mysteries and of beauty of meaning, is the sixth in the order of the twelve Prophets. Setting a short prologue before his book, he shows the time of his prophesying, saying: [[1:1|The word of the Lord, that came to Micah, the Morasthite|Verbum Domini quod factum est ad Michæam Morasthiten]], that is, the prophetic discourse spoken by God through an angel to Micheas, a native of Morasthi, a little village situated near Eleutheropolis, a city of Palestine, [[1:1|in the days of Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda|in diebus Joathan, Achaz et Ezechiæ regum Juda]]. He does not set down the names of the kings of Israel, that is, of the ten tribes, under whom he prophesied, because once the kings of Juda, whose reigns were contemporary with theirs, are named, these are easily understood. It was also said above that Osee[[Osee 1:1||]] and Amos[[Amos 1:1||]], and indeed Isaias too[[Is 1:1||]], prophesied under Ozias, Joathan, Achaz and Ezechias. But this Micheas is not read to have prophesied under Ozias, the father of Joathan. From which it is gathered that Micheas began to prophesy under Joathan, and in part prophesied at the same time as Osee, Isaias and Amos, though he began after them. From this it is further plain that this Micheas is another than the one of whom we read in the third book of Kings, who prophesied under Achab[[3 Kings 22:8||]], and of whom Achab said to Josaphat: [[3 Kings 22:8|I hate him, for he doth not prophecy good to me, but evil|Ego odi eum, quia non prophetat mihi nisi malum]]. That one, then, long preceded this Micheas, and was called [[3 Kings 22:8|Micheas, the son of Jemla|Michæas filius Jemla]].

paras.t: Quod vidit, id est, spiritualiter intellexit in repræsentatione visionis imaginariæ : intelligentia siquidem opus est in visione ; super Samariam, id est de populo decem tribuum, quæ nomine Samariæ designantur, quia Samaria fuit in regno illo metropolis. Posset tamen Samaria accipi pro ipsa provincia. Et Jerusalem, id est de populo duarum tribuum, scilicet Juda et Benjamin : sub quibus comprehenditur tribus sacerdotalis atque Levitica, quæ a tempore separationis decem tribuum a domo David, adhæsit regno David, in quo fuit templum et cultus divinus. Decem enim tribus fecerunt sibi sacerdotes de extremis populorum. Per Jerusalem ergo metropolim regni Juda, signantur hæ tribus. Denique Michæas de utroque regno prophetavit : et primo de decem tribuum populo, ideo exprimit Samariam ante Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[1:1|which he saw|Quod vidit]], that is, understood spiritually in the representation of an imaginary vision [that is, a vision of images formed in the imagination, as distinct from a bodily or a purely intellectual one]: for [[Dan 10:1|there is need of understanding in a vision|intelligentia siquidem opus est in visione]]; [[1:1|concerning Samaria|super Samariam]], that is, about the people of the ten tribes, who are designated by the name of Samaria, because Samaria was the chief city of that kingdom. Samaria could, however, be taken for the province itself. [[1:1|and Jerusalem|Et Jerusalem]], that is, about the people of the two tribes, namely Juda and Benjamin, under which is included the priestly and Levitical tribe, which, from the time when the ten tribes separated from the house of David, adhered to the kingdom of David[[2 Par 11:13||]][[2 Par 11:14||]], in which were the temple and the worship of God. For the ten tribes made themselves [[3 Kings 12:31|priests of the lowest of the people|sacerdotes de extremis populorum]]. By Jerusalem, then, the chief city of the kingdom of Juda, these tribes are signified. Lastly, Micheas prophesied about both kingdoms, and first about the people of the ten tribes; therefore he names Samaria before Jerusalem.

paras.t: Hoc ergo verbum Domini ostensum Michæ, est quod subjungitur. Antequam tamen verbum istud describitur, excitat Propheta auditores ad diligentissimam advertentiam dicendorum. Verba enim altissima cum multa sunt reverentia auscultanda. Audite auribus cordis et corporis, populi omnes, et attendat terra et plenitudo ejus. Ad litteram Propheta loquitur hoc ad duodecim tribus. Et per terram intelligit habitatores utriusque regni ; plenitudo autem intelligi possunt meliores aut ditiores. Vel repetit idem sub aliis verbis, sicut frequenter fit in Scripturis ad ampliorem attentionem excitandam. Et sit Dominus Deus vobis in testem, id est, Deus sit vobis testis veritatis eorum quæ dico, scilicet testificando seu demonstrando quod vera sint quæ loquor. Unde Symmachus transtulit, Testificans ; et Septuaginta transtulerunt, In testimonium. Vel sensus est, quod Deus attestetur Prophetæ quod annuntiavit populo quæ Deus præcepit : quatenus populus si non obedierit, nullam habeat excusationem, Deo contra ipsum testimonium perhibente, qui ait in Jeremia : Ego sum judex et testis. Hoc modo Moyses ait in Deuteronomio : Contestabor contra vos cœlum et terram. Dominus de templo sancto suo, id est, de cœlo ita testetur, puta de cœlo empyreo, in quo specialiter esse et habitare asseritur : ideo quoque dicitur inde operari. Vel templum Dei sanctum, vocatur electorum fidelis collectio, in quibus gratiose habitat.
paras.en: This word of the Lord shown to Micheas, then, is what follows. Before that word is set out, however, the Prophet rouses his hearers to the most careful attention to what is to be said; for the loftiest words are to be listened to with great reverence. [[1:2|Hear|Audite]] with the ears of heart and body, [[1:2|all ye people: and let the earth give ear, and all that is therein|populi omnes, et attendat terra et plenitudo ejus]]. Literally, the Prophet says this to the twelve tribes. By *the earth* he understands the inhabitants of both kingdoms, while by its *fulness* [the Latin *plenitudo*, which the Douay-Rheims renders “all that is therein”] the better or the richer can be understood. Or he repeats the same thing in other words, as is often done in the Scriptures to rouse fuller attention. [[1:2|and let the Lord God be a witness to you|Et sit Dominus Deus vobis in testem]], that is, let God be a witness to you of the truth of what I say, namely by testifying or showing that what I speak is true. Hence Symmachus translated *Testifying*, and the Septuagint *For a testimony*. Or the sense is that God bears witness for the Prophet that he has announced to the people what God commanded, so that if the people do not obey they may have no excuse, since God bears witness against them, who says in Jeremias: [[Jer 29:23|I am the judge and the witness|Ego sum judex et testis]]. In this way Moses says in Deuteronomy: I [[Deut 31:28|will call heaven and earth to witness|Contestabor contra vos cœlum et terram]] against you. [[1:2|the Lord from his holy temple|Dominus de templo sancto suo]], that is, let Him so bear witness from heaven, namely from the empyrean heaven, in which He is especially said to be and to dwell; and so He is also said to work from there. Or the holy temple of God is the name given to the faithful assembly of the elect, in whom He dwells by grace.

paras.t: Deinde ponitur verbum Dei propheticum huic vati ostensum. Quia ecce Dominus egredietur de loco suo, id est, de sublimi cœlorum habitaculo descendet ad terram, non in se, vel per aliquam sui motionem aut loci mutationem, sed per operationem seu ultionem, atque potentiæ suæ declarationem. Ibi enim Deus esse asseritur, ubi evidenter operatur. Dum ergo non ostendit potestatem suam in impiis, eorum ulciscendo peccata, videtur deesse ; dum vero vindicat, dicitur visitare, venire, sive accedere. Unde habetur in Psalmo: Domine, inclina cœlos tuos et descende. In Genesi quoque Dominus ait de Sodomitis : Descendam, et videbo si juxta clamorem qui venit ad me, faciant. Vel locus immensi Dei, est ipsemet Deus. Infinitum enim fulcit se ipsum, nec aliquid extra se continet illud. Deus quoque lucem habitat inaccessibilem. Dum ergo Deus omnipotens se ipsum non manifestat, quasi in proprio permanet loco. Dum vero suam virtutem vel sapientiam sive justitiam manifestat per effectus, egredi fertur de loco suo, id est de sui ipsius abscondito. De quo loquitur Isaias : Vere tu es Deus absconditus. Rursus, quum natura Dei sit bonitas, proprium ei est et connaturale, esse propitium seu misereri et parcere : sicque locus Dei est misericordia ejus. Dum ergo a dulcedine pietatis transit ad æquitatis rigorem, et durum atque severum se exhibet propter nostra delicta (quod quasi alienum ab eo est), egreditur de loco suo. Et descendet, per ultionis effectum, et calcabit super excelsa terræ, id est, colla terrenorum et impiorum suppeditabit, tradendo idololatras filios Israel manibus et pedibus adversariorum, puta Assyriorum et Chaldæorum.
paras.en: Next is set down the prophetic word of God shown to this seer. [[1:3|For behold the Lord will come forth out of his place|Quia ecce Dominus egredietur de loco suo]], that is, He will come down from the lofty dwelling of the heavens to the earth: not in Himself, nor by any movement of His own or change of place, but by His working, or vengeance, and the showing of His power. For God is said to be there where He evidently works. So while He does not show His power upon the wicked by avenging their sins, He seems to be absent; but when He punishes, He is said to visit, to come, or to draw near. Hence we have in the Psalm: [[Ps 143:5|Lord, bow down thy heavens and descend|Domine, inclina cœlos tuos et descende]]. In Genesis too the Lord says of the Sodomites: [[Gen 18:21|I will go down and see whether they have done according to the cry that is come to me|Descendam, et videbo si juxta clamorem qui venit ad me, faciant]]. Or the place of the immense God is God Himself. For the infinite upholds itself, and nothing outside itself contains it. God, too, [[1 Tim 6:16|inhabiteth light inaccessible|lucem habitat inaccessibilem]]. So while almighty God does not manifest Himself, He abides as it were in His own place; but when He manifests His power, or wisdom, or justice, through their effects, He is said to come forth out of His place, that is, out of His own hiddenness. Of which Isaias speaks: [[Is 45:15|Verily thou art a hidden God|Vere tu es Deus absconditus]]. Again, since the nature of God is goodness, it is proper and connatural to Him to be propitious, that is, to have mercy and to spare; and so the place of God is His mercy. So when He passes from the sweetness of His loving-kindness to the rigour of justice, and shows Himself hard and severe because of our sins (which is, as it were, foreign to Him), He comes forth out of His place. [[1:3|and he will come down|Et descendet]], by the effect of vengeance, [[1:3|and will tread upon the high places of the earth|et calcabit super excelsa terræ]], that is, He will trample on the necks of the earthly and the wicked, delivering the idolatrous children of Israel into the hands and under the feet of their adversaries, namely the Assyrians and the Chaldeans.

paras.t: Et consumentur montes subter eum, id est, majores, utpote reges seu principes, sacerdotes et judices, occidentur divina virtute ab hostibus jam præfatis ; et valles, id est inferiores, scindentur, id est, destruentur ab inimicis valde velociter, sicut cera a facie, id est præsenti calore, ignis consumitur, et sicut aquæ quæ decurrunt in præceps, id est, a loco altiori fluunt in bassiorem. Tales enim aquæ dividuntur in guttas seu rivulos.
paras.en: [[1:4|And the mountains shall be melted under him|Et consumentur montes subter eum]], that is, the greater, such as kings or princes, priests and judges, shall be slain by the power of God at the hands of the enemies just named; [[1:4|and the valleys|et valles]], that is, the lower, [[1:4|shall be cleft|scindentur]], that is, shall be destroyed by their enemies very swiftly, [[1:4|as wax before|sicut cera a facie]], that is, by the present heat of, [[1:4|the fire|ignis]] is consumed, [[1:4|and as waters that run down a steep place|et sicut aquæ quæ decurrunt in præceps]], that is, flow from a higher place to a lower; for such waters are divided into drops or rivulets.

paras.t: In scelere Jacob, id est propter idololatriam decem tribuum, quæ nomine patris sui Jacob exprimuntur, omne istud, id est, tota punitio ista infligitur, et in peccatis domus Israel, id est etiam propter alias iniquitates populi Israel, seu decem tribuum, quæ dicuntur Jacob et Israel, quemadmodum pater earum dictus est Jacob et Israel. Vel Jacob et Israel, possunt referri ad regnum Juda et Samariæ. Quod scelus Jacob præcipuum ? nonne Samaria, id est idololatria quæ in metropoli illa vigebat, vel majores qui alios ad vitia induxerunt, fueruntque peccatum, id est causa inductiva peccati, subjectis. Et quæ excelsa Judæ, id est fana seu loca sublimia, in quibus duæ tribus idololatriam exercebant? nonne Jerusalem, id est excelsa quæ in metropoli Juda, puta Jerusalem, exstiterunt, vel circa eam ? Exemplo enim regum qui in Jerusalem idololatriam commiserunt, ceteri de regno Juda inducti fuerunt ad idem sub pluribus regibus Juda, præsertim sub Achaz et Manasse, ut patet in libro Regum.
paras.en: [[1:5|For the wickedness of Jacob|In scelere Jacob]], that is, because of the idolatry of the ten tribes, who are expressed by the name of their father Jacob, [[1:5|is all this|omne istud]], that is, all this punishment is inflicted, [[1:5|and for the sins of the house of Israel|et in peccatis domus Israel]], that is, also because of the other iniquities of the people of Israel, or of the ten tribes, which are called Jacob and Israel[[Num 24:5||]][[Ps 80:5||]], just as their father was called Jacob[[Gen 25:25||]] and Israel[[Gen 32:28||]]. Or Jacob and Israel can be referred to the kingdom of Juda and that of Samaria. [[1:5|What is the wickedness of Jacob?|Quod scelus Jacob]] What is his chief one? [[1:5|is it not Samaria?|nonne Samaria]] That is, the idolatry that flourished in that chief city; or the great men who led others into vice and were a *sin* to their subjects, that is, a cause leading them into sin. [[1:5|and what are the high places of Juda?|Et quæ excelsa Judæ]] That is, the shrines or lofty places in which the two tribes practised idolatry. [[1:5|are they not Jerusalem?|nonne Jerusalem]] That is, the high places that stood in the chief city of Juda, namely Jerusalem, or around it. For by the example of the kings who committed idolatry in Jerusalem, the rest of the kingdom of Juda were led to the same under several kings of Juda, especially under Achaz[[4 Kings 16:1||]] and Manasses[[4 Kings 21:1||]], as is plain in the book of Kings.

paras.t: Et ponam Samariam quasi acervum lapidum in agro, id est, metropolim decem tribuum per Assyrios destruam, ita quod ædificia corruentia, erunt velut congeries saxorum positorum in agris, quum plantatur vinea circa agrum. Tunc enim lapides de loco vineæ colliguntur, et in unum cumulum projiciuntur. Et detraham per Assyrios in vallem lapides ejus, id est structuras lapideas Samariæ, quæ sita fuit in montibus, et fundamenta ejus revelabo, id est, funditus destruetur, in tantum ut fundamenta cernantur sub terra.
paras.en: [[1:6|And I will make Samaria as a heap of stones in the field|Et ponam Samariam quasi acervum lapidum in agro]], that is, I will destroy the chief city of the ten tribes through the Assyrians, so that its fallen buildings shall be like a pile of stones laid in the fields, [[1:6|when a vineyard is planted|quum plantatur vinea]] round about the field: for then the stones are gathered from the place of the vineyard and thrown together into one heap. [[1:6|and I will bring down|Et detraham]] through the Assyrians [[1:6|the stones thereof into the valley|in vallem lapides ejus]], that is, the stone buildings of Samaria, which was situated on hills, [[1:6|and will lay her foundations bare|et fundamenta ejus revelabo]], that is, it shall be utterly destroyed, so much so that the foundations are seen beneath the ground.

paras.t: Et omnia sculptilia ejus, id est idola sculpta, concidentur, id est, ab Assyriis destruentur, ut quidquid pretiosum fuerit in idolis, tollant, sive aurum sive argentum. Et omnes mercedes ejus, id est possessiones, quas cives Samariæ putabant sibi dari ab idolis pro præmio servitutis exhibitæ idolis : de quibus dictum est in Osee, Mercedes hæ meæ, quas dederunt mihi amatores mei, id est dii quibus amorose servivi; comburentur igni, illæ videlicet quas Assyrii non consumpserunt, nec asportare quiverunt. Et omnia idola ejus ponam in perditionem : ita quod destruentur ab hostibus, nec se, nec suos cultores valebunt defendere; quia de mercedibus meretricis, id est de divitiis Samariæ spiritualiter fornicantis cum diis (vel tota gens duodecim tribuum, idolorum cultrix, dicitur meretrix, recedendo a Deo vero, et cum idolis fornicando), congregata sunt, id est, conflata atque collecta sunt idola. Ex pretiosis namque materiis fabricati sunt idola. Unde per Isaiam et Osee Deus conqueritur, quod ex auro et argento suo, quod scilicet ipse concessit filiis Israel, ipsi deos seu idola perfecerunt. Et usque ad mercedem meretricis, id est Ninive seu gentis Assyriæ corporaliter et spiritualiter fornicantis, revertentur, id est, in potestatem Assyriorum redigentur : qui quidquid pretiosum et placitum invenerunt in idolis Samariæ, secum tulerunt in Niniven, quasi pro mercede pugnæ suæ contra decem tribus. Imo Deus talia dedit eis pro obsequio quo sibi contra decem pessimas tribus servierunt, eo modo quo ad Ezechielem ait, quod regi ac populo Babylonis dabit bona Ægypti pro mercede obsequii quo sibi contra Tyrum servierunt, quia in Tyro pauca repererunt. Hæc omnia contigerunt decem tribubus maxime tempore Osee regis Israel, ut legitur quarto Regum. Nomine quoque Samariæ urbis metropolitanæ, aliæ urbes decem tribuum intelliguntur.
paras.en: [[1:7|And all her graven things|Et omnia sculptilia ejus]], that is, the carved idols, [[1:7|shall be cut in pieces|concidentur]], that is, shall be destroyed by the Assyrians, so that they may carry off whatever was precious in the idols, whether gold or silver. [[1:7|and all her wages|Et omnes mercedes ejus]], that is, the possessions which the citizens of Samaria thought were given them by the idols as a reward for the service they showed the idols; of which it is said in Osee: [[Osee 2:12|These are my rewards, which my lovers have given me|Mercedes hæ meæ, quas dederunt mihi amatores mei]] [the Latin word is the same, *mercedes*: “rewards” there, “wages” here], that is, the gods whom I served with love; [[1:7|shall be burnt with fire|comburentur igni]], namely those which the Assyrians did not consume and could not carry away. [[1:7|and I will bring to destruction all her idols|Et omnia idola ejus ponam in perditionem]]: so that they shall be destroyed by the enemy, and shall be able to defend neither themselves nor their worshippers; for [[1:7|of the hire of a harlot|de mercedibus meretricis]], that is, from the riches of Samaria committing spiritual fornication with the gods (or the whole nation of the twelve tribes, a worshipper of idols, is called a harlot, for departing from the true God and fornicating with idols), [[1:7|they were gathered together|congregata sunt]], that is, the idols were cast and collected. For the idols were made of precious materials. Hence through Isaias[[Is 46:6||]] and Osee[[Osee 2:8||]][[Osee 8:4||]] God complains that out of His gold and silver, that is, what He Himself had granted to the children of Israel, they made gods or idols. [[1:7|and unto the hire of a harlot|Et usque ad mercedem meretricis]], that is, of Ninive, or of the Assyrian nation committing fornication bodily and spiritually, [[1:7|they shall return|revertentur]], that is, they shall be brought into the power of the Assyrians, who carried off with them to Ninive whatever they found precious and pleasing in the idols of Samaria, as the wages of their fighting against the ten tribes. Indeed God gave them such things for the service with which they served Him against the ten most wicked tribes, in the way in which He says to Ezechiel that He will give the goods of Egypt to the king and people of Babylon as wages for the service with which they served Him against Tyre[[Ezech 29:18||]][[Ezech 29:19||]][[Ezech 29:20||]], since they found little in Tyre. All this befell the ten tribes chiefly in the time of Osee king of Israel, as we read in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 17:6||]]. By the name of Samaria, the chief city, the other cities of the ten tribes are also understood.

paras.t: Super hoc, id est de tanta miseria et pressura decem tribuum, plangam et ululabo ex magna compassione. Vadam spoliatus societate populi mei, vel propriis bonis. Assyrii enim etiam justorum bona diripiebant. Et nudus, id est pauper. Vel hoc ideo dicit, quoniam secundum consuetudinem Judæorum, tempore tantæ tribulationis vestimenta propria laceravit; vel ad placandum Dominum, captivitate instante, per nuditatem se ipsum afflixit in pœnitentia pro aliis. Faciam planctum velut draconum, id est altum atque horribilem, quemadmodum dracones, quum ab elephantis vincuntur, terribili perstrepunt sibilo, et luctum quasi struthionum, id est valde miserabilem. Struthio autem, sicut in Job dicitur, duratur ad fetus suos, et ovorum suorum immemor, relinquit ea in arena, transeuntium pedibus conculcanda. Nihilo minus orta occasione plurimum dolens, suo modo luctum emittit.
paras.en: [[1:8|Therefore|Super hoc]] [literally “over this”], that is, over so great a misery and oppression of the ten tribes, [[1:8|will I lament, and howl|plangam et ululabo]] out of great compassion. [[1:8|I will go stript|Vadam spoliatus]] of the company of my people, or of my own goods; for the Assyrians plundered the goods of the just as well. [[1:8|and naked|Et nudus]], that is, poor. Or he says this because, after the custom of the Jews, in a time of such great tribulation he tore his own garments; or because, to appease the Lord as the captivity drew near, he afflicted himself by nakedness in penance for others. [[1:8|I will make a wailing like the dragons|Faciam planctum velut draconum]], that is, loud and dreadful, as dragons, when they are overcome by elephants, roar with a terrible hiss; [[1:8|and a mourning like the ostriches|et luctum quasi struthionum]], that is, most pitiful. Now the ostrich, as is said in Job[[Job 39:13||]], [[Job 39:16|is hardened against her young ones|duratur ad fetus suos]], and, unmindful of her eggs, leaves them in the sand[[Job 39:14||]] to be trodden under the feet of passers-by[[Job 39:15||]]. Nevertheless, when occasion arises, grieving greatly, she sends forth a mourning in her own way.

paras.t: Quia desperata est plaga ejus : id est, iniquitas decem tribuum, quæ est animæ vulnus, insanabilis est, ob suam radicationem in cordibus impiorum, et obdurationem ac incorrigibilitatem peccantium, qui abjecerunt Prophetas, et converti spreverunt, quamvis absolute loquendo, non fuerit incurabilis. Vel, Plaga ejus, id est punitio seu captivitas populi hujus, desperata est, id est inconvertibilis et irrevocabilis, ita quod veniam non meretur, et usque in […] finem mundi durabit. Hoc modo scriptum est apud Jeremiam : Quid clamas ad me? insanabilis est dolor tuus : et in Osee, Non addam ut diligam eos. Hæc est una ratio tanti ploratus. Alia est, quia venit usque ad Judam, id est, culpa et pœna decem tribuum, usque ad regnum duarum tribuum venit : quia similia crimina operantes duæ tribus, quæ decem, talia passæ sunt a Chaldæis, qualia decem ab Assyriis. Tetigit portam populi mei, id est, persecutio Chaldæorum portas urbium Juda destruxit, usque ad Jerusalem inclusive, quia illam quoque destruxerunt Chaldæi. Vel, Usque ad Jerusalem exclusive : et tunc de Sennacherib rege Assyriorum et ejus exercitu intelligendum est, qui ascendit super omnes urbes Juda, et obtinuit eas, sicut habetur in Isaia.
paras.en: [[1:9|Because her wound is desperate|Quia desperata est plaga ejus]]: that is, the iniquity of the ten tribes, which is a wound of the soul, is incurable, because it is rooted in the hearts of the wicked, and because of the hardness and incorrigibility of the sinners, who cast off the Prophets and scorned to be converted; though, speaking absolutely, it was not incurable. Or, [[1:9|her wound|Plaga ejus]], that is, the punishment or captivity of this people, [[1:9|is desperate|desperata est]], that is, cannot be turned back or revoked, so that it does not earn pardon, and shall last until […] the end of the world. So it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 30:15|Why criest thou|Quid clamas]] to me? [[Jer 30:15|thy sorrow is incurable|insanabilis est dolor tuus]] [Denis has *ad me*, “to me”, where the Vulgate has *super contritione tua*, “for thy affliction”]; and in Osee: [[Osee 9:15|I will love them no more|Non addam ut diligam eos]]. This is one reason for such great weeping. The other is, [[1:9|because it is come even to Juda|quia venit usque ad Judam]], that is, the guilt and the punishment of the ten tribes came even to the kingdom of the two tribes: for the two tribes, committing crimes like those of the ten, suffered from the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:1||]] such things as the ten suffered from the Assyrians[[4 Kings 17:6||]]. [[1:9|it hath touched the gate of my people|Tetigit portam populi mei]], that is, the persecution of the Chaldeans destroyed the gates of the cities of Juda, [[1:9|even to Jerusalem|usque ad Jerusalem]] inclusive, since the Chaldeans destroyed it too[[4 Kings 25:9||]][[4 Kings 25:10||]]. Or, *even to Jerusalem* exclusive: and then it is to be understood of Sennacherib king of the Assyrians and his army, who went up against all the cities of Juda and took them, as we have in Isaias[[Is 36:1||]] [no margin reference here; the passage is Is 36:1].

paras.t: In Geth urbe Philistinorum, nolite annuntiare plagam populi Israel, ne vitiose lætentur Philistæi, qui semper oderunt Israeliticam plebem. Unde occisis Saul et Jonatha, David cecinit : Nolite nuntiare in Geth, ne exsultent incircumcisi. Lacrimis ne ploretis, id est, plangendo nolite interioris tristitiæ signa ostendere, nec in singultibus dolor erumpat, ne rumor ad Philistæos deveniat. In domo pulveris, id est occulte in domibus ad luctum aptis, in quibus solent pulveres lugentium capitibus superjactari; vel per domum pulveris intelligit habitacula ruinosa, quæ quilibet ingredi potest, ut lugeat in secreto ; pulvere vos conspergite, id est, pulveres superponite capiti vestro : quemadmodum consuetudo fuit Judæis tempore angustiæ, superjactare capitibus pulveres, in signum doloris et humilitatis, juxta illud in Psalmo : Quoniam humiliata est in pulvere anima nostra.
paras.en: [[1:10|in Geth|In Geth]], a city of the Philistines, [[1:10|Declare ye it not|nolite annuntiare]] the wound of the people of Israel, lest the Philistines, who always hated the Israelite people, rejoice wickedly. Hence, when Saul and Jonathan had been slain, David sang: [[2 Kings 1:20|Tell it not in Geth|Nolite nuntiare in Geth]], [[2 Kings 1:20|lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph|ne exsultent incircumcisi]]. [[1:10|weep ye not with tears|Lacrimis ne ploretis]], that is, do not show signs of inward sorrow by lamenting, nor let your grief break out in sobs, lest the report reach the Philistines. [[1:10|in the house of Dust|In domo pulveris]], that is, secretly, in houses suited to mourning, in which dust is usually thrown upon the heads of mourners; or by the house of dust he understands ruined dwellings, which anyone may enter to mourn in secret; [[1:10|sprinkle yourselves with dust|pulvere vos conspergite]], that is, put dust upon your heads; as it was the custom of the Jews in a time of distress to cast dust upon their heads in sign of grief and humility, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 43:25|For our soul is humbled down to the dust|Quoniam humiliata est in pulvere anima nostra]].

paras.t: Transite vobis, id est, ad vestram confusionem in captivitatem transibitis, habitatio pulchra, id est, Samaritani seu decem tribus habitantes in Samaria, quæ sita fuit in pulcherrimo atque uberrimo loco Judææ : habitatio, inquam, confusa ignominia, id est, ignominiosis confusionibus impleta. Confusibiliter enim Assyrii tractaverunt hanc gentem. Non est egressa, id est nondum de terra sua translata, quæ habitat in exitu, plebs hæc exsistens in foribus captivitatis, seu quasi in janua exeundi, quia jam protinus capietur. Vel sensus est, quod non est egressa sponte, sed violenter et tracta. Planctum domus vicinæ accipiet ex vobis, quæ stetit sibimet. Iste est sensus et ordo verborum : Quæ stetit sibimet, id est, domus regni Juda, quæ, destructa Samaria, sub Ezechia adhuc stetit firma sub protectione divina, quoniam tempore Ezechiæ Deo servivit, accipiet ex vobis, id est vestro exemplo, o decem tribubus, planctum domus vicinæ, id est causam lugendi taliter ut vos luxistis. Domus enim vicina dicitur regnum decem tribuum, quod proximum fuit regno Juda. Regnum vero Juda tempore Manassæ imitabatur peccata et idololatriam decem tribuum : sicque sumpsit ex eis causam suæ punitionis a Chaldæis, quam sustinendo, deplanxit. Vel est sensus, quod aliqui ex duabus tribubus audientes decem tribuum captivitatem, condoluerunt, et sibimetipsis metuebant plangentes.
paras.en: [[1:11|And pass away|Transite vobis]] [literally “pass over for yourselves”], that is, you shall pass into captivity to your own confusion, [[1:11|O thou that dwellest in the beautiful place|habitatio pulchra]] [literally “beautiful dwelling”], that is, the Samaritans, or the ten tribes dwelling in Samaria, which was situated in a most beautiful and fertile spot of Judea: a dwelling, I say, [[1:11|covered with thy shame|confusa ignominia]], that is, filled with shameful confusions; for the Assyrians treated this nation shamefully. [[1:11|she went not forth|Non est egressa]], that is, she has not yet been carried away from her land, [[1:11|that dwelleth in the confines|quæ habitat in exitu]] [*in exitu*, literally “at the going out”]: this people, standing at the doors of captivity, as it were on the threshold of going out, since she will be taken very soon. Or the sense is that she did not go out of her own accord, but by force, and dragged. [[1:11|the house adjoining shall receive mourning from you|Planctum domus vicinæ accipiet ex vobis]], [[1:11|which stood by herself|quæ stetit sibimet]]. This is the sense and order of the words: [[1:11|which stood by herself|Quæ stetit sibimet]], that is, the house of the kingdom of Juda, which, when Samaria was destroyed[[4 Kings 18:9||]][[4 Kings 18:10||]], still stood firm under Ezechias under the protection of God, since in the time of Ezechias it served God, [[1:11|shall receive mourning from you|accipiet ex vobis]], that is, by your example, O ten tribes, *the mourning of the neighbouring house* [Denis reads *planctum domus vicinæ*, “the mourning of the neighbouring house”; the Vulgate has *domus vicina*, “the neighbouring house”, as the subject], that is, cause for mourning such as you mourned. For the kingdom of the ten tribes is called the neighbouring house, because it was next to the kingdom of Juda. But the kingdom of Juda in the time of Manasses imitated the sins and the idolatry of the ten tribes, and so took from them the cause of its punishment by the Chaldeans, and in enduring it lamented. Or the sense is that some of the two tribes, hearing of the captivity of the ten tribes, grieved with them, and lamented in fear for themselves.

paras.t: Quia infirmata est in bonum, id est, a bono et cultu divino dejecta est, quæ habitat in amaritudinibus, id est domus regni Juda insistens peccatis, Deum ad amaritudinem provocantibus; vel, habitans in pœnis, quas propter sua peccata incurrit. Quia descendit malum a Domino, id est, punitionem Deus adduxit per Assyrios seu Chaldæos, in portam Jerusalem, quam destruxerunt Chaldæi. Unde Dominus ait per Jeremiam : Ecce ego assumam servum meum Nabuchodonosor ; et convocabo regna Babylonis, et venient, et ponent unusquisque solium suum in portis Jerusalem. Rex quoque Assyriorum de Lachis misit Rabsacen cum manu gravi ad Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[1:12|For she is become weak unto good|Quia infirmata est in bonum]], that is, she is cast down from good and from the worship of God, [[1:12|that dwelleth in bitterness|quæ habitat in amaritudinibus]], that is, the house of the kingdom of Juda, persisting in sins that provoke God to bitterness; or, dwelling in the punishments which she incurred for her sins. [[1:12|for evil is come down from the Lord|Quia descendit malum a Domino]], that is, God brought punishment through the Assyrians or the Chaldeans, [[1:12|into the gate of Jerusalem|in portam Jerusalem]], which the Chaldeans destroyed. Hence the Lord says through Jeremias: Behold I will take my servant Nabuchodonosor[[Jer 25:9||]], and I will call together the kingdoms of Babylon, [[Jer 1:15|and they shall come, and shall set every one his throne|et venient, et ponent unusquisque solium suum]] in [[Jer 1:15|the gates of Jerusalem|portis Jerusalem]] [no margin reference here; Denis's words join Jer 25:9 (or 43:10) and Jer 1:15]. Also [[Is 36:2|the king of the Assyrians sent Rabsaces from Lachis to Jerusalem|Rex quoque Assyriorum de Lachis misit Rabsacen cum manu gravi ad Jerusalem]] with a heavy hand [no margin reference here; the words are those of Is 36:2, cf. 4 Kings 18:17].

paras.t: Tumultus quadrigæ stuporis, id est strepitus quadrigarum seu curruum hostilium, ad stuporem mentis inducentium, incutiendo magnum timorem, venit habitanti Lachis, id est habitatoribus civitatis sic dictæ, quam vastavit Sennacherib, qua capta, perrexit contra Lobnam. Et sic ista exponuntur de Assyriis et Lachis urbe Juda. Alii vero exponunt de Chaldæis et Lachis, quæ alio nomine dicta est Dan, fuitque sita in termino aquilonari terræ promissionis, per quam Chaldæi cum curribus et equitibus intraverunt contra Judæam. Principium peccati est filiæ Sion. Hoc secundum primam præcedentis clausulæ expositionem ita accipitur : Lachis quæ fuit in regno Juda, fuit principium peccati et idololatriæ filiæ Sion, id est urbi Jerusalem et Judææ, seu populo Juda communiter, quia in te, o Lachis, inventa sunt scelera Israel, id est idololatria vitiaque annexa decem tribuum, et ita per te, velut per portam, intraverunt regnum Juda. Quoad secundam præcedentis clausulæ interpretationem, iste est sensus, quod Lachis quæ dicta est Dan, fuit principium idololatriæ regno Juda, quoniam in Lachis a tempore judicum fuit idolum Michæ, ut dicitur in libro Judicum : et ita ex Lachis derivata est idololatria ad decem tribus, a quibus ultra processit ad duas. Hæc tamen expositio videtur ambigua, quia Jeroboam filius Nabat, rediens ex Ægypto, cœpit idololatriam in decem tribubus : quam non didicit in Lachis seu Dan. Verumtamen in Dan fuit unus vitulorum aureorum, sicque quodammodo fuit decem tribubus principium hujus facinoris.
paras.en: [[1:13|A tumult of chariots hath astonished|Tumultus quadrigæ stuporis]] [literally “the tumult of the chariot of astonishment”], that is, the din of the four-horse chariots, or war-cars, of the enemy, which bring the mind to astonishment by striking it with great fear, comes upon [[1:13|the inhabitants of Lachis|habitanti Lachis]], that is, upon the inhabitants of the city so named, which Sennacherib laid waste, and, having taken it, went on against Lobna[[4 Kings 19:8||]]. And so these words are expounded of the Assyrians and of Lachis, a city of Juda. Others, however, expound them of the Chaldeans and of Lachis [the edition notes that this should be *Lais*][[Judg 18:29||]], which by another name was called Dan, and lay on the northern border of the land of promise[[Is 10:30||]], through which the Chaldeans entered against Judea with chariots and horsemen. [[1:13|it is the beginning of sin to the daughter of Sion|Principium peccati est filiæ Sion]]. According to the first exposition of the preceding clause, this is taken thus: Lachis, which was in the kingdom of Juda, was the beginning of sin and of idolatry to the daughter of Sion, that is, to the city of Jerusalem and to Judea, or to the people of Juda in general, [[1:13|for in thee|quia in te]], O Lachis, [[1:13|were found the crimes of Israel|inventa sunt scelera Israel]], that is, the idolatry of the ten tribes and the vices joined to it; and so through thee, as through a gate, they entered the kingdom of Juda. As to the second interpretation of the preceding clause, the sense is this: that Lachis, which was called Dan, was the beginning of idolatry to the kingdom of Juda, since in Lachis from the time of the judges there was the idol of Michas, as is said in the book of Judges[[Judg 18:7||]] [the margin gives Judg. xviii, 7–29; the idol is set up in Dan at Judg 18:30–31]; and so idolatry spread from Lachis to the ten tribes, and from them went on further to the two. This exposition, however, seems doubtful, because Jeroboam the son of Nabat, returning out of Egypt[[3 Kings 12:2||]], began idolatry in the ten tribes[[3 Kings 12:28||]], and he did not learn it in Lachis or Dan. Yet in Dan was one of the golden calves[[3 Kings 12:29||]], and so in a manner it was to the ten tribes the beginning of this crime.

paras.t: Propterea, id est propter vitia nunc expressa, aut similia, dabit rex Assyriorum, vel Deus per illum mittet, emissarios, id est pugnatores sive latrunculos, vel sagittarios, super hereditatem Geth, id est contra urbem metropolim Philistinorum nomine Geth, et contra divitias ejus : quæ urbs et cujus habitatores fuerunt domus mendacii in deceptionem regibus Israel, id est, reges Israel mentiendo deceperunt, sicque meruerunt hanc pœnam.
paras.en: [[1:14|Therefore|Propterea]], that is, because of the vices just expressed, or the like, [[1:14|shall she send|dabit]] [the Latin *dabit*, literally “shall give”]: that is, the king of the Assyrians shall give, or God through him shall send, [[1:14|messengers|emissarios]], that is, fighters or raiders, or archers, [[1:14|to the inheritance of Geth|super hereditatem Geth]], that is, against Geth, the chief city of the Philistines, and against its riches; which city and whose inhabitants were [[1:14|the houses of lying to deceive the kings of Israel|domus mendacii in deceptionem regibus Israel]], that is, they deceived the kings of Israel by lying, and so deserved this punishment.

paras.t: Adhuc heredem, id est alienos heredes seu hostes Assyrios, bona tua rapientes ac possidentes, adducam tibi, plebs Israel, quæ habitas in Maresa, id est urbe sic appellata. Usque ad Odollam, id est habitatores civitatis illius ad terram promissionis pertinentis, veniet gloria Israel, id est ignominiosa captivitas decem tribuum, quia et ipsi ab Assyriis capti sunt. Loquitur autem Propheta ironice, intelligendo per gloriam Israel, confusionem ipsius, quemadmodum Michol ait ad David : Quam gloriosus fuit rex Israel hodie!
paras.en: [[1:15|Yet|Adhuc]] [[1:15|an heir|heredem]], that is, foreign heirs, the Assyrian enemies, seizing and possessing thy goods, [[1:15|will I bring|adducam]] [[1:15|to thee|tibi]], O people of Israel, [[1:15|that dwellest in Maresa|quæ habitas in Maresa]], that is, in the city so called. [[1:15|even to Odollam|Usque ad Odollam]], that is, to the inhabitants of that city, which belonged to the land of promise, [[1:15|shall the glory of Israel come|veniet gloria Israel]], that is, the shameful captivity of the ten tribes, since they too were taken by the Assyrians[[4 Kings 17:6||]]. Now the Prophet speaks ironically, meaning by the glory of Israel its confusion, as Michol said to David: [[2 Kings 6:20|How glorious was the king of Israel to day|Quam gloriosus fuit rex Israel hodie]]!

paras.t: Decalvare et tondere, id est, o Samaria et Israel, cui tanta confusio imminet, depone ornatum, et more captivorum radere ignominiose, in signum calamitatis tuæ atque tristitiæ, super filios deliciarum tuarum, id est propter captivitatem filiorum tuorum, qui aliquando deliciosi fuerunt et delicate nutriti; dilata calvitium tuum, id est, magna sit decalvatio tua tonsioque præfata, sicut aquila, cui excidunt plumæ ob vetustatem; quoniam captivi ducti sunt ex te, id est, filii tui mox in captivitatem ducentur. Imo tempore hujus prophetiæ jam multi fuerunt capti et pressi seu interfecti sub regibus Assyriorum Phul et Theglathphalasar.
paras.en: [[1:16|Make thee bald, and be polled|Decalvare et tondere]], that is, O Samaria and Israel, over whom so great a confusion hangs, lay aside thy adornment, and after the manner of captives be shamefully shaven, in sign of thy calamity and sorrow, [[1:16|for thy delicate children|super filios deliciarum tuarum]], that is, because of the captivity of thy sons, who were once delicate and daintily nourished; [[1:16|enlarge thy baldness|dilata calvitium tuum]], that is, let thy baldness and the shearing just named be great, [[1:16|as the eagle|sicut aquila]], whose feathers fall out from age; [[1:16|for they are carried into captivity from thee|quoniam captivi ducti sunt ex te]], that is, thy sons shall soon be led into captivity. Indeed at the time of this prophecy many had already been taken and oppressed, or slain, under the kings of the Assyrians, Phul[[4 Kings 15:19||]] and Theglathphalasar[[4 Kings 15:29||]].

paras.t: Postremo hanc expositionem litteralem atque consimiles dicit se ab Hebræis didicisse S. Hieronymus.
paras.en: Lastly, St Jerome says that he learned this literal exposition, and others like it, from the Hebrews.

1.title: Elucidatio moralis ejusdem primi capituli.
1.title_en: Moral explanation of the same first chapter.

paras.t: Michæas interpretatur humilitas; Morasthi vero, heres. Qui igitur humilitate ornatur, discens semper a Christo quoniam mitis est et humilis corde, et ad cœlestis pertinet hereditatis sortem, cui præparavit Deus quæ oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, nec ratio comprehendit : hic talis illustratur a Spiritu Sancto, fitque ad eum verbum Domini, et audit quid loquatur in ipso Dominus Deus, quoniam divino instinctui acquiescit. Hinc Salomon ait : Ubi humilitas, ibi et sapientia. Nempe, quo homo se ipsum Deo profundius humiliusque supponit, eo Deus gratiosius ad ipsum convertitur, et vacuitatem ejus liberalius implet, quia humilitas in veritate fundatur. Et quanto se aliquis verius perfectiusque dignoscit, eo se declivius, timoratius, atque intimius deprimit, ac per hoc æternæ et increatæ Veritati carior fit atque propinquior. Propter quod ait Salvator : Qui se humiliat, exaltabitur. In libro Job quoque inducitur : Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria. Itaque, si virtute et gratia radicari, si radio sapientiæ illustrari, si Deo dilecti, vicini ac intimi esse optamus, humiliemur ex toto corde sub potenti manu Dei, cujus comparatione est totus mundus tanquam pulvis exiguus.
paras.en: Micheas is interpreted *humility*, and Morasthi *heir*. He, then, who is adorned with humility, ever learning from Christ that he is [[Matt 11:29|meek, and humble of heart|mitis est et humilis corde]], and who belongs to the lot of the heavenly inheritance, for which God hath prepared what [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard|oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit]], nor reason comprehended[[Is 64:4||]]: such a one is enlightened by the Holy Ghost, and [[1:1|the word of the Lord|verbum Domini]] comes to him, and he hears [[Ps 84:9|what the Lord God will speak|quid loquatur in ipso Dominus Deus]] in him, because he yields to the divine prompting. Hence Solomon says: [[Prov 11:2|where humility is, there also is wisdom|Ubi humilitas, ibi et sapientia]]. For the more deeply and humbly a man places himself beneath God, the more graciously God turns to him and the more liberally he fills his emptiness, because humility is founded on truth. And the more truly and perfectly a man knows himself, the lower, the more fearfully and the more inwardly he abases himself, and by this he becomes dearer and nearer to the eternal and uncreated Truth. Wherefore the Saviour says: [[Luke 14:11|he that humbleth himself shall be exalted|Qui se humiliat, exaltabitur]][[Luke 18:14||]]. In the book of Job too it is set down: [[Job 22:29|he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory|Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria]]. And so, if we long to be rooted in virtue and grace, to be enlightened by the ray of wisdom, to be loved by God, near to him and intimate with him, let us humble ourselves with our whole heart [[1 Pet 5:6|under the mighty hand of God|sub potenti manu Dei]], in comparison with whom the whole world is [[Is 40:15|as a little dust|tanquam pulvis exiguus]].

paras.t: Denique humilis jam præfatus videt verbum Domini super Samariam, id est fictos et reprobos Christianos, qui dicunt se nosse et diligere Christum, factis autem negant. Samaria vero interpretatur custodia : per quod designantur virtuosi in propriis oculis, simulatores vani atque hypocritæ, qui se Christi legem jactant servare. Quid ergo de istis dicat Dominus, audit et noscit humilis a Deo instructus, quoniam de talibus novit scriptum : Simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei; et, Non veniet in conspectu Dei omnis hypocrita. De quibus ait Salvator : Væ vobis, qui similes estis sepulcris dealbatis, quæ a foris parent hominibus speciosa, intus vero plena sunt ossibus mortuorum et omni spurcitia : sic et vos quidem a foris paretis hominibus justi, intus vero pleni estis hypocrisi et omni iniquitate. Proinde simulata æquitas non est æquitas, sed duplex iniquitas.
paras.en: Next, the humble man spoken of above sees [[1:1|the word of the Lord|verbum Domini]] [[1:1|concerning Samaria|super Samariam]], that is, concerning feigned and reprobate Christians, who say that they know and love Christ, but [[Tit 1:16|in their works they deny him|factis autem negant]]. Samaria is interpreted *watch* [*custodia*, a guard or keeping]: by which are signified those who are virtuous in their own eyes, vain dissemblers and hypocrites, who boast that they keep the law of Christ. What, then, the Lord says of these, the humble man taught by God hears and knows, since he knows that it is written of such: [[Job 36:13|Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God|Simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei]]; and, [[Job 13:16|no hypocrite shall come before his presence|Non veniet in conspectu Dei omnis hypocrita]]. Of whom the Saviour says: [[Matt 23:27|Woe to you|Væ vobis]], who [[Matt 23:27|are like to whited sepulchres, which outwardly appear to men beautiful but within are full of dead men's bones and of all filthiness|similes estis sepulcris dealbatis, quæ a foris parent hominibus speciosa, intus vero plena sunt ossibus mortuorum et omni spurcitia]]: [[Matt 23:28|So you also outwardly indeed appear to men just: but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.|sic et vos quidem a foris paretis hominibus justi, intus vero pleni estis hypocrisi et omni iniquitate]] Hence feigned equity is not equity, but a double iniquity.

paras.t: Et Jerusalem : id est, talis quoque intelligit quid de electorum Ecclesia Deus pronuntiet, scilicet, quod omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur; et quod omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tentationes transierunt fideles. Talibus quippe ait Salvator : Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur, quia non est servus major domino suo. Et denuo ait : Mundus gaudebit; vos autem contristabimini, sed tristitia vestra vertetur in gaudium, et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis.
paras.en: [[1:1|and Jerusalem|Et Jerusalem]]: that is, such a man also understands what God pronounces concerning the Church of the elect: namely, that [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ|omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo]] [[2 Tim 3:12|shall suffer persecution|persecutionem patientur]]; and that [[Jdt 8:23|all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tentationes transierunt fideles]] [Denis reads *temptations* where the Vulgate has *tribulations*]. For to such the Saviour says: [[John 15:20|If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you|Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur]], because [[John 15:20|The servant is not greater than his master|non est servus major domino suo]]. And again he says: [[John 16:20|the world shall rejoice: and you shall be made sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy|Mundus gaudebit; vos autem contristabimini, sed tristitia vestra vertetur in gaudium]]; [[John 16:22|And your joy no man shall take from you|et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis]].

paras.t: Audite, populi omnes, et attendat terra, id est Ecclesia militans degens in isto exsilio, et plenitudo ejus, id est gratiæ spirituales concessæ fidelibus, scilicet virtutes, et dona Spiritus Sancti : quatenus procedant ad actum, dum verbum Dei proponitur. Et sit Dominus Deus vobis in testem, id est, Christus, qui est testis fidelis, sit testificans contra vos, si male egeritis; et pro vobis, si bene.
paras.en: [[1:2|Hear, all ye people: and let the earth give ear|Audite, populi omnes, et attendat terra]], that is, the Church militant dwelling in this exile, [[1:2|and all that is therein|et plenitudo ejus]] [literally *and the fulness thereof*], that is, the spiritual graces granted to the faithful, namely the virtues and the gifts of the Holy Ghost: so that they may go forth into act when the word of God is set forth. [[1:2|and let the Lord God be a witness to you|Et sit Dominus Deus vobis in testem]], that is, let Christ, who is [[Apoc 1:5|the faithful witness|testis fidelis]], bear witness against you if you do ill, and for you if you do well.

paras.t: Quia ecce Dominus Christus egredietur de loco suo, id est de summo cœlo in die judicii ; et descendet secundum naturam assumptam, et calcabit super excelsa terræ, id est, superba hujus mundi dejiciet. Unde in Ecclesiastico : Omnium, inquit, excellentium et sublimium colla calcavi; et in Proverbiis, Arrogantiam et superbiam, viam pravam et os bilingue detestor. Hinc in Jeremia præcipitur : Nolite elevari; sed date gloriam Domino Deo vestro, antequam contenebrescat, et antequam offendant pedes vestri ad montes caliginosos. Præterea, intra bonos et humiles calcat Deus, quoniam in illorum cordibus habitat, ambulat, epulatur; sed supra superbos et malos calcat, quoniam deprimit, spernit, et damnat ejusmodi. Nec solum intra electos et humiles calcat Deus, sed insuper quasi supponit se eis, dicente Psalmista de electo : Quum ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus supponit manum suam; et Moyse in Deuteronomio, Portavit te Dominus Deus tuus, sicut portare solet homo filium suum. O quanta unio atque communio Dei sublimis, et servuli humilis!
paras.en: [[1:3|For behold the Lord|Quia ecce Dominus]], Christ, [[1:3|will come forth out of his place|egredietur de loco suo]], that is, from the highest heaven on the day of judgment; [[1:3|and he will come down|et descendet]] according to the nature he assumed, [[1:3|and will tread upon the high places of the earth|et calcabit super excelsa terræ]], that is, he will cast down the proud things of this world. Whence in Ecclesiasticus he says: [[Ecclus 24:11|I have trodden under my feet the hearts of all the high|excellentium et sublimium colla calcavi]] [Denis reads: of all the excellent and the lofty I have trodden the necks; a note in the edition gives the variant *corda*, hearts, which is the Vulgate's word]; and in Proverbs: [[Prov 8:13|I hate arrogance, and pride, and every wicked way, and a mouth with a double tongue|Arrogantiam et superbiam, viam pravam et os bilingue detestor]]. Hence it is commanded in Jeremias: [[Jer 13:15|Be not proud|Nolite elevari]]; but [[Jer 13:16|Give ye glory to the Lord your God, before it be dark, and before your feet stumble upon the dark mountains|date gloriam Domino Deo vestro, antequam contenebrescat, et antequam offendant pedes vestri ad montes caliginosos]]. Moreover, God treads within the good and humble, since he dwells, walks and feasts in their hearts; but he treads upon the proud and wicked, since he brings such men low, spurns them and condemns them. And God not only treads within the elect and humble, but moreover as it were puts himself beneath them, as the Psalmist says of the elect man: [[Ps 36:24|When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, for the Lord putteth his hand under him.|Quum ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus supponit manum suam]] and Moses in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 1:31|the Lord thy God hath carried thee, as a man is wont to carry his little son|Portavit te Dominus Deus tuus, sicut portare solet homo filium suum]]. O how great is the union and communion of the sublime God and his humble little servant!

paras.t: Et consumentur montes, et valles scindentur : id est, universi superbi, et terrenis rebus immersi, qui valles dicuntur (de quibus loquitur Jeremias, Recedentes a te, in terra scribentur), peribunt.
paras.en: [[1:4|And the mountains shall be melted|Et consumentur montes]], [[1:4|and the valleys shall be cleft|et valles scindentur]]: that is, all the proud, and those sunk in earthly things, who are called valleys (of whom Jeremias speaks: [[Jer 17:13|they that depart from thee, shall be written in the earth|Recedentes a te, in terra scribentur]]), shall perish.

paras.t: In scelere Jacob, id est propter peccata fidelium, omne istud : propter culpam enim infligitur pœna. Propter quod scriptum est in Job : Recordare, obsecro, quis unquam innocens periit? Quin potius vidi iniquos Domino flante periisse. Quod scelus Jacob, id est ecclesiasticorum et electorum virorum? nonne Samaria, id est id ad quod a perversis inducuntur? a quibus frequenter pertrahuntur ad vitia, dicente Scriptura : Cum perverso perverteris; et, Qui tetigerit picem, inquinabitur. Unde in Numeris Moyses loquitur : Recedite a tabernaculis hominum impiorum, et nolite tangere quæ ad illos pertinent, ne involvamini in peccatis eorum. Hinc gratulabundus et gratus concinit Psalmista : Protexisti me a conventu malignantium, a multitudine operantium iniquitatem.
paras.en: [[1:5|For the wickedness of Jacob|In scelere Jacob]], that is, on account of the sins of the faithful, [[1:5|is all this|omne istud]]: for punishment is inflicted on account of guilt. Wherefore it is written in Job: [[Job 4:7|Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished being innocent|Recordare, obsecro, quis unquam innocens periit]]? [[Job 4:8|On the contrary, I have seen|Quin potius vidi]] the wicked [[Job 4:9|perishing by the blast of God|Domino flante periisse]]. [[1:5|What is the wickedness of Jacob|Quod scelus Jacob]], that is, of churchmen and of chosen men? [[1:5|is it not Samaria|nonne Samaria]], that is, that to which they are led on by the perverse, by whom they are often drawn away into vices? As Scripture says: [[Ps 17:27|with the perverse thou wilt be perverted|Cum perverso perverteris]]; and, [[Ecclus 13:1|He that toucheth pitch, shall be defiled|Qui tetigerit picem, inquinabitur]]. Whence in Numbers Moses says: [[Num 16:26|Depart from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest you be involved in their sins|Recedite a tabernaculis hominum impiorum, et nolite tangere quæ ad illos pertinent, ne involvamini in peccatis eorum]]. Hence the Psalmist sings with thanksgiving and gratitude: [[Ps 63:3|Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant; from the multitude of the workers of iniquity.|Protexisti me a conventu malignantium, a multitudine operantium iniquitatem]]

paras.t: Et quæ excelsa Judæ, id est animositates et vanitates confitentium Deo, seu Christianorum bonorum? Qui licet sint perseverantes in gratia, tamen subinde superbiæ vanitatisque sentiunt motus. Nonne Jerusalem, id est illæ ad quas exemplo superiorum ac prælatorum inducuntur, qui in Ecclesia sortiuntur primatum, sicut Jerusalem erat in Judæa metropolis? Dum enim subjecti conspiciunt tales pompatice ingredi, vanitatibus occupari, et intimorate coram Altissimo conversari; tunc et ipsi ad aliqua mala labuntur, vel superiores incaute judicando, vel eos in illicitis imitando, vel ex ignorantia prævaricando, quia non erant a suis edocti prælatis.
paras.en: [[1:5|and what are the high places of Juda|Et quæ excelsa Judæ]], that is, the haughtiness and vanities of those who confess God, or of good Christians? For though they persevere in grace, they nevertheless feel from time to time the stirrings of pride and vanity. [[1:5|are they not Jerusalem|Nonne Jerusalem]], that is, those into which they are led by the example of their superiors and prelates, who hold the first place in the Church, as Jerusalem was the chief city of Judæa? For when subjects see such men going about with pomp, taken up with vanities, and living without fear before the Most High, then they too slip into some evils: either by judging their superiors rashly, or by imitating them in what is unlawful, or by transgressing out of ignorance, because they had not been taught by their prelates.

paras.t: Et ponam Samariam, id est reprobos, quasi acervum lapidum : quando in fine sæculi ligabuntur fasciculi et fasciculi, et congregati congregatione unius fascis, simul projicientur in tartarum, ibique recludentur in carcere. Et detraham in vallem infernalis laci lapides ejus, id est duritiam cordis, vel fortitudinem de qua præsumpsit; aut certe virtutes quas se jactavit aut simulavit habere, quæ non erant veræ virtutes, sed lutum et fæces. Idcirco, quum veniens Christus illuminaverit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestaverit consilia cordium, cognoscentur vere ab omnibus : tuncque clarissime comprehendentur astuti in astutia eorum. Et fundamenta ejus, id est vanitates in quibus se fundavit, revelabo, id est, omnibus notificabo, ut agnoscant æquitatem judicii mei. Hi siquidem tanquam stulti, ædificant domum suam super arenam : idcirco veniente fluvio, ventoque flante, cadit structura.
paras.en: [[1:6|And I will make Samaria|Et ponam Samariam]], that is, the reprobate, [[1:6|as a heap of stones|quasi acervum lapidum]]: when at the end of the world they shall be bound up bundle by bundle[[Matt 13:30||]], and, [[Is 24:22|gathered together as in the gathering of one bundle|congregati congregatione unius fascis]], shall be cast together into Tartarus, and [[Is 24:22|they shall be shut up there in prison|ibique recludentur in carcere]]. [[1:6|and I will bring down the stones thereof into the valley|Et detraham in vallem infernalis laci lapides ejus]] [Denis reads: into the valley of the pit of hell], that is, its hardness of heart, or the strength in which it presumed; or indeed the virtues which it boasted or pretended to have, which were not true virtues but mud and dregs. Therefore, when Christ comes, who [[1 Cor 4:5|will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts|illuminaverit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestaverit consilia cordium]], these will be truly known by all; and then the crafty will be caught most plainly in their own craftiness. [[1:6|her foundations|Et fundamenta ejus]], that is, the vanities on which she founded herself, I will lay [[1:6|bare|revelabo]], that is, I will make them known to all, so that they may acknowledge the justice of my judgment. For these, like fools, build their [[Matt 7:26|house upon the sand|domum suam super arenam]]: therefore, when the flood comes and the wind blows, the building falls[[Matt 7:27||]].

paras.t: Et omnia sculptilia ejus, id est verba composita, ornatus superfluus, excogitatæ doctrinæ fallaces, concidentur. Et omnes mercedes ejus, id est divitiæ contra jus acquisitæ per artificia prava, laudes quoque et honores ab hominibus exhibiti eis, comburentur igni, id est, damnationi faciendo eos obnoxios. Opera enim illorum sequuntur illos. Propterea scriptum est in Isaia : Erit fortitudo impiorum ut favilla stuppæ, et opus quasi scintilla; et succendetur utrumque simul. Et omnia idola ejus, id est simulacra : de quibus ait Joannes, Custodite vos a simulacris, scilicet vanis cogitationibus, inutilibus phantasiis, formis imaginibusque nocivis, quæ mentem depingunt et maculant, atque a stabili divinorum contemplatione præpediunt; ponam in perditionem, id est, condemnabo ac puniam. Quia de mercedibus meretricis, id est animæ a cœlesti Sponso aversæ, congregata sunt. Anima enim meretur gratia privari : quo facto, incidit et colligit sibi plurima mala, quæ sunt culpa et pœna culpæ. Et usque ad mercedem meretricis, id est diabolicæ ac infernalis congregationis incessabiliter a Deo se avertentis, revertentur : id est, operatores iniquitatum istarum a dæmonibus possidebuntur velut mercedes, quas diu tentando et impugnando adepti sunt.
paras.en: [[1:7|And all her graven things|Et omnia sculptilia ejus]], that is, studied words, superfluous adornment, devised and deceitful doctrines, [[1:7|shall be cut in pieces|concidentur]]. [[1:7|and all her wages|Et omnes mercedes ejus]], that is, riches gained against right by wicked arts, and also the praises and honours shown them by men, [[1:7|shall be burnt with fire|comburentur igni]], that is, by making them liable to damnation. For [[Apoc 14:13|their works follow them|Opera enim illorum sequuntur illos]]. Therefore it is written in Isaias: [[Is 1:31|your strength shall be as the ashes of tow, and your work as a spark: and both shall burn together|Erit fortitudo impiorum ut favilla stuppæ, et opus quasi scintilla; et succendetur utrumque simul]] [Denis reads *the strength of the wicked* for *your strength*]. [[1:7|all her idols|Et omnia idola ejus]], that is, images [*simulacra*], of which John says, [[1 John 5:21|keep yourselves from idols|Custodite vos a simulacris]]: namely vain thoughts, useless fancies, harmful forms and images, which paint and stain the mind and hinder it from the steady contemplation of divine things; [[1:7|I will bring to destruction|ponam in perditionem]], that is, I will condemn and punish. For [[1:7|of the hire of a harlot|de mercedibus meretricis]], that is, of the soul turned away from the heavenly Bridegroom, [[1:7|they were gathered together|congregata sunt]]. For the soul deserves [*meretur*, echoing *meretrix*, harlot] to be deprived of grace; and when this is done, it falls into and gathers to itself very many evils, which are guilt and the punishment of guilt. [[1:7|and unto the hire of a harlot|Et usque ad mercedem meretricis]], that is, of the devilish and hellish congregation that ceaselessly turns itself away from God, [[1:7|they shall return|revertentur]]: that is, the workers of these iniquities shall be possessed by the demons as wages, which these have won by long tempting and assailing.

paras.t: Super hoc plangam et ululabo, pereuntibus cordialiter condolendo, et iniquorum duritiam deplorando : sicut Apostolo tristitia magna fuit et dolor continuus, pro fratribus suis impœnitentibus incredulisque Judæis. Qui iterum loquitur : Quis infirmatur, et ego non infirmor? Quis scandalizatur, et ego non uror? Vadam spoliatus et nudus, id est frustratus spe mea de illorum salvatione, vel in paupertate ac nuditate pœnitentiam agens. Faciam planctum velut draconum. Quanto enim anima est nobilior corpore, et quanto æterna damnatio gravior est omni temporali supplicio, tanto vehementius dolendum ac flendum est de animarum periculo et damnatione perpetua, quam de corporum ægrotatione, seu quacumque temporali afflictione.
paras.en: [[1:8|Therefore will I lament, and howl|Super hoc plangam et ululabo]], grieving from the heart with those who perish and bewailing the hardness of the wicked: as the Apostle had [[Rom 9:2|great sadness and continual sorrow|tristitia magna fuit et dolor continuus]] for his brethren[[Rom 9:3||]], the impenitent and unbelieving Jews. And again he says: [[2 Cor 11:29|Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is scandalized, and I am not on fire?|Quis infirmatur, et ego non infirmor? Quis scandalizatur, et ego non uror?]] [[1:8|I will go stript and naked|Vadam spoliatus et nudus]], that is, frustrated in my hope of their salvation, or doing penance in poverty and nakedness. [[1:8|I will make a wailing like the dragons|Faciam planctum velut draconum]]. For as much as the soul is nobler than the body, and as much as eternal damnation is heavier than any temporal punishment, so much the more vehemently must we grieve and weep over the peril of souls and their everlasting damnation than over the sickness of bodies or any temporal affliction.

paras.t: Quia desperata est plaga ejus. Hoc de peccatis in Spiritum Sanctum specialiter accipi potest, quæ in tantum desperata sunt, quantum et irremissibilia. Nam et impius quum in profundum venerit peccatorum, contemnit. Et Apostolus ait : Hæreticum hominem post unam et secundam correptionem devita, sciens quia subversus est, et delinquit proprio judicio condemnatus. Quum ergo homines caritate flagrantes viderint quempiam durum et incorrigibilem, maxime dolent, nec cessant. Sed dum desperant se posse in illo proficere, jugi supplicatione convertuntur ad Deum, ut cor lapideum auferat, et mentem immutet.
paras.en: [[1:9|Because her wound is desperate|Quia desperata est plaga ejus]]. This may be taken especially of the sins against the Holy Ghost, which are as desperate as they are unpardonable [*irremissibilia*: they are called so because they reject the very things by which sin is forgiven, not because God's mercy cannot reach them]. For [[Prov 18:3|The wicked man, when he is come into the depths of sins, contemneth|impius quum in profundum venerit peccatorum, contemnit]]. And the Apostle says: [[Tit 3:10|A man that is a heretic, after the first and second admonition, avoid:|Hæreticum hominem post unam et secundam correptionem devita]] [[Tit 3:11|Knowing that|sciens quia]] he [[Tit 3:11|is subverted and sinneth, being condemned by his own judgment|subversus est, et delinquit proprio judicio condemnatus]]. When, therefore, men burning with charity see someone hard and incorrigible, they grieve exceedingly and do not cease; but when they despair of being able to do him any good, they turn to God in unceasing prayer, that he may take away the heart of stone and change the mind.

paras.t: Quia venit usque ad Judam, id est, quosdam de Ecclesia infecit pravitas malignorum ; tetigit portam populi mei, id est prælatos, qui esse debent aliis via et janua introeundi ad Christum, tanquam mediatores inter Deum et nos, usque ad Jerusalem, id est supremos pastores, in tantum ut sicut populus sic sacerdotes.
paras.en: [[1:9|because it is come even to Juda|Quia venit usque ad Judam]], that is, the depravity of the wicked has infected some in the Church; [[1:9|it hath touched the gate of my people|tetigit portam populi mei]], that is, the prelates, who ought to be to others the way and the door by which to enter to Christ, as mediators between God and us, [[1:9|even to Jerusalem|usque ad Jerusalem]], that is, the chief pastors; so much so that [[Is 24:2|as with the people, so with the priest|sicut populus sic sacerdotes]][[Osee 4:9||]].

paras.t: In Geth, id est persecutoribus Christianorum, nolite annuntiare plagas Ecclesiæ, ne Christum blasphement, et de fidelium adversitatibus glorientur. Geth autem interpretatur torcular : quo oppressores justorum significantur. Lacrimis ne ploretis in publico, ne illi percipiant et exsultent. In domo pulveris, id est locis abditis et humilibus, pulvere vos conspergite, id est, in secreto vos humiliate, flete, et pœnitentiam agite, præsertim de peccatis occultis, ut cum Psalmista dicatis : Similis factus sum pelecano solitudinis ; factus sum sicut nycticorax in domicilio.
paras.en: [[1:10|in Geth|In Geth]], that is, to the persecutors of Christians, [[1:10|Declare ye it not|nolite annuntiare]], the wounds of the Church, lest they blaspheme Christ and glory in the adversities of the faithful. Now Geth is interpreted *winepress*: by which the oppressors of the just are signified. [[1:10|weep ye not with tears|Lacrimis ne ploretis]] in public, lest they perceive it and exult. [[1:10|in the house of Dust|In domo pulveris]], that is, in hidden and lowly places, [[1:10|sprinkle yourselves with dust|pulvere vos conspergite]], that is, humble yourselves in secret, weep, and do penance, especially for hidden sins, so that you may say with the Psalmist: [[Ps 101:7|I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness: I am like a night raven in the house.|Similis factus sum pelecano solitudinis ; factus sum sicut nycticorax in domicilio]]

paras.t: Transite vobis, habitatio pulchra : id est, qui in mundo isto floretis ac prosperamini, in damnationem transibitis, nisi pœniteatis : idcirco transite de vitiis ad virtutes, de terrenis ad divina, de multis ad unum, de creaturis ad Creatorem ; confusa ignominia, id est, qui nunc a dæmonibus turpiter fallimini, et ignominiosis peccatis subdimini. Non est egressa, quæ habitat in exitu : id est, congregatio iniquorum, quæ statim de sæculo isto ad aliud perget, non egreditur de pristina conversatione injusta, et de amore sensibilium ad contemplationem cœlestium, nec novissima sua perpendit ; sed sic vivit, quasi moritura non esset, sola præsentia atque mundana curando. Planctum domus vicinæ accipiet ex vobis, quæ stetit sibimet : id est, virtuosi in virtutibus permanentes, ex ruina et damnatione proximorum suorum perversorum lugebunt.
paras.en: [[1:11|pass away, O thou that dwellest in the beautiful place|Transite vobis, habitatio pulchra]]: that is, you who flourish and prosper in this world will pass into damnation unless you repent; therefore pass from vices to virtues, from earthly things to divine, from many things to one[[Luke 10:42||]], from creatures to the Creator; [[1:11|covered with thy shame|confusa ignominia]], that is, you who are now shamefully deceived by the demons and made subject to shameful sins. [[1:11|she went not forth that dwelleth in the confines|Non est egressa, quæ habitat in exitu]] [*in exitu*, literally at the going out, which Denis takes of the passing out of this world]: that is, the congregation of the wicked, which will presently pass from this world to another, does not go forth from its former unjust way of life, nor from the love of the things of sense to the contemplation of heavenly things, nor does it weigh its last end; but it lives as though it were not going to die, caring only for things present and worldly. [[1:11|the house adjoining shall receive mourning from you, which stood by herself|Planctum domus vicinæ accipiet ex vobis, quæ stetit sibimet]]: that is, the virtuous, who abide in virtue, will mourn over the ruin and damnation of their perverse neighbours.

paras.t: Quia infirmata est in bonum, id est, a bono defecit, nec in opera virtuosa viriliter fortiterque processit, quæ habitat in amaritudinibus, id est peccatis seu afflictionibus, de quibus loquitur Job : Scribis enim contra me amaritudines.
paras.en: [[1:12|For she is become weak unto good|Quia infirmata est in bonum]], that is, has fallen away from good and has not gone forward manfully and bravely into virtuous works, [[1:12|that dwelleth in bitterness|quæ habitat in amaritudinibus]], that is, in sins or afflictions, of which Job speaks: [[Job 13:26|For thou writest bitter things against me|Scribis enim contra me amaritudines]] [*amaritudines*, the same word as *bitterness* in the verse].

paras.t: Tumultus quadrigæ stuporis, id est multitudo tentationis diabolicorum spirituum obstupefacientium corda, ne sentiant ea quæ sunt Spiritus Dei, veniet habitanti Lachis, id est vagis et intimoratis, qui ambulant in vanitate sensus sui, nec stabiliuntur in Deo : de quibus fertur in Psalmo, In circuitu impii ambulant ; et, Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam. Lachis autem interpretatur ambulatio. Hinc ad cordis stabilitatem ubertim hortatur nos divinus Apostolus, secundum quod ait ad Corinthios : Stabiles estote et immobiles, abundantes in omni opere bono ; alibi quoque, Optimum, inquit, est gratia stabiliri cor.
paras.en: [[1:13|A tumult of chariots hath astonished|Tumultus quadrigæ stuporis]] [literally *the tumult of the chariot of stupor*], that is, the multitude of the temptation of devilish spirits that stupefy hearts, so that they perceive not the [[1 Cor 2:14|things that are of the Spirit of God|ea quæ sunt Spiritus Dei]], shall come to [[1:13|the inhabitants of Lachis|habitanti Lachis]], that is, to the wandering and to those without fear of God, who [[Eph 4:17|walk in the vanity of their mind|ambulant in vanitate sensus sui]] and are not made steadfast in God: of whom it is said in the Psalm, [[Ps 11:9|The wicked walk round about|In circuitu impii ambulant]]; and, [[Ps 82:14|O my God, make them like a wheel|Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam]]. Now Lachis is interpreted *walking*. Hence the divine Apostle exhorts us abundantly to stability of heart, as he says to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 15:58|be ye steadfast and unmoveable|Stabiles estote et immobiles]], abounding in every good work; and elsewhere: [[Heb 13:9|it is best|Optimum]], he says, [[Heb 13:9|that the heart be established with grace|est gratia stabiliri cor]].

paras.t: Hinc secundum Philosophum, ad sapientes et virtuosos præcipue spectat stabilitas mentis. Instabilitas vero, insipientiæ signum est : et competit his qui passionibus agitantur atque vincuntur, debilesque consistunt in judicio rationis. Debemus ergo rationem divina lege instructam immobiliter sequi, passionumque inhonestissimis impulsionibus dominari. Nec tamen esse debemus duri et pertinaces, ut illi qui suam pertinaciam asserunt stabilitatem.
paras.en: Hence, according to the Philosopher [Aristotle], stability of mind belongs above all to the wise and virtuous. Instability, on the other hand, is a sign of folly, and befits those who are driven about and overcome by the passions, and are weak in the judgment of reason. We ought therefore to follow reason, instructed by the divine law, without wavering, and to master the most shameful impulses of the passions. Yet we must not be hard and obstinate, like those who call their obstinacy stability.

paras.t: Denique Lachis, id est instabilitas ista et evagatio cordis, principium peccati est filiæ Sion, id est animabus fidelibus ; quæ nisi omni diligentia enitantur figi in Deo, plurima crimina illabuntur. Propter quod scriptum est in Proverbiis : Omni custodia custodi cor tuum, quia ex ipso vita procedit ; et in Ecclesiastico : Non ventiles te in omnem ventum ; esto firmus in via Domini, et in veritate sensus tui, et prosequatur te verbum pacis.
paras.en: Lastly, Lachis, that is, this instability and wandering of the heart, is [[1:13|the beginning of sin to the daughter of Sion|principium peccati est filiæ Sion]], that is, to faithful souls; for unless they strive with all diligence to be fixed in God, they slip into very many crimes. Wherefore it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 4:23|With all watchfulness keep thy heart, because life issueth out from it.|Omni custodia custodi cor tuum, quia ex ipso vita procedit]] and in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 5:11|Winnow not with every wind|Non ventiles te in omnem ventum]]; [[Ecclus 5:12|Be steadfast in the way of the Lord, and in the truth of thy judgment|esto firmus in via Domini, et in veritate sensus tui]], [[Ecclus 5:12|and let the word of peace|et prosequatur te verbum pacis]] follow thee.

paras.t: Propterea dabit Dominus emissarios, id est diabolos impugnatores, super hereditatem Geth, id est incircumcisos corde, qui velut torcular opprimunt bonos, et meliores se vexant : quum hi qui in gravioribus culpis sunt, non debeant accusare, punire, vel judicare eos qui minus culpabiles sunt, secundum Ambrosium, præsertim quum in Evangelio dicat Salvator : Hypocrita, ejice primum trabem de oculo tuo, et tunc perspicies ut ejicias festucam de oculo fratris tui. Hi autem Gethitæ sunt domus mendacii, id est filii falsitatis, agentes contra veritatem vitæ, justitiæ, atque doctrinæ, in deceptionem regibus Israel, id est prælatorum Ecclesiæ, vel hominum virtuosorum, qui regunt se ipsos in omnibus secundum divinæ legis directionem ac normam. Tales namque interdum falluntur et subvertuntur ab illis.
paras.en: [[1:14|Therefore shall she send|Propterea dabit]] [Denis reads: Therefore shall the Lord send] [[1:14|messengers|emissarios]], that is, devils who assail, [[1:14|to the inheritance of Geth|super hereditatem Geth]], that is, upon the uncircumcised in heart, who like a winepress crush the good and harass those better than themselves: whereas, according to Ambrose, those who are in graver faults ought not to accuse, punish or judge those who are less guilty; above all since the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Matt 7:5|Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thy own eye, and then shalt thou see to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.|Hypocrita, ejice primum trabem de oculo tuo, et tunc perspicies ut ejicias festucam de oculo fratris tui]] These men of Geth are [[1:14|the houses of lying|domus mendacii]], that is, sons of falsehood, acting against the truth of life, of justice and of doctrine, [[1:14|to deceive the kings of Israel|in deceptionem regibus Israel]], that is, the prelates of the Church, or virtuous men, who rule themselves in all things according to the direction and rule of the divine law. For such men are sometimes deceived and overthrown by them.

paras.t: Adhuc heredem adducam tibi, quæ habitas in Maresa. Dum aliquis a malis conversus, Deo adhæret, fit Christus heres seu possessor ipsius ; si vero ad vomitum redeat, et peccatis subjiciatur, possidetur a dæmone. Usque ad Odollam, id est haurientes mala et observatores malorum, veniet gloria Israel (ironice), id est confusio Christianorum injustorum. Qui enim observator est malorum, opprimetur ab eis. Odolla autem interpretatur, testimonium hauritionis eorum. Et in Proverbiis legitur : Fili, si malus fueris, solus hauries mala.
paras.en: [[1:15|Yet will I bring an heir to thee that dwellest in Maresa|Adhuc heredem adducam tibi, quæ habitas in Maresa]]. When anyone, turned away from evil, cleaves to God, Christ becomes his heir or possessor; but if he returns to his vomit and is made subject to sins, he is possessed by the devil. [[1:15|even to Odollam|Usque ad Odollam]], that is, to those who draw up evils [*haurire*, to draw, as water, or to drink in] and watch for evils, [[1:15|shall the glory of Israel come|veniet gloria Israel]] (ironically), that is, the confusion of unjust Christians.
