paras.t: Qui ædificatis Sion, id est domus vestras in Jerusalem, in sanguinibus, id est de rapinis pauperum, cæde insontium, occisione sanctorum, quorum substantiam diripientes, construitis habitacula vestra; et Jerusalem, id est urbem ipsam, ædificatis in iniquitate, id est de rebus illicite acquisitis, quas a subditis extorquetis, et exinde ruinas urbis reparatis.
paras.en: [[3:10|You that build up Sion|Qui ædificatis Sion]], that is, your houses in Jerusalem, [[3:10|with blood|in sanguinibus]], that is, out of the plunder of the poor, the slaughter of the innocent, the killing of the saints, whose substance you seize to put up your dwellings; [[3:10|and Jerusalem|et Jerusalem]], that is, the city itself, you build [[3:10|with iniquity|in iniquitate]], that is, out of things unlawfully gained, which you extort from your subjects, and with them you repair the ruins of the city.

paras.t: Principes ejus in muneribus judicabant, id est, propter dona dabant injustas sententias ; vel si juste judicabant, magis adspexerunt ad commodum temporale quam ad bonum spirituale, vendebantque sententiam, nec stipendio sui laboris erant recta intentione contenti. Et sacerdotes ejus in mercede docebant populum, id est, propter lucrum directe, spirituale pro temporali exhibentes : quum tamen ex officio haberent instruere plebem gratis, ad Dei honorem et animarum salutem; temporalia non quærentes, nisi secundario tanquam stipendium vitæ. Et prophetæ ejus in pecunia divinabant, id est, pseudo propter nummos mendosa vaticinia protulerunt. Propter quod dicitur in Isaia : Omnes diligunt munera, sequuntur retributionem ; et in Jeremia, A propheta usque ad sacerdotem cuncti faciunt dolum.
paras.en: [[3:11|Her princes have judged for bribes|Principes ejus in muneribus judicabant]], that is, for gifts they gave unjust sentences; or, if they judged justly, they looked more to temporal advantage than to spiritual good, and sold their sentence, and were not content, with a right intention, with the wage of their labour. [[3:11|and her priests have taught for hire|Et sacerdotes ejus in mercede docebant]] the people, that is, directly for gain, offering the spiritual for the temporal: whereas by their office they were bound to instruct the people freely, for the honour of God and the salvation of souls, not seeking temporal things except secondarily, as a living wage. [[3:11|and her prophets divined for money|Et prophetæ ejus in pecunia divinabant]], that is, the false ones uttered lying oracles for coin. Wherefore it is said in Isaias: [[Is 1:23|they all love bribes, they run after rewards|Omnes diligunt munera, sequuntur retributionem]]; and in Jeremias: [[Jer 6:13|from the prophet even to the priest, all are guilty of deceit|A propheta usque ad sacerdotem cuncti faciunt dolum]].

paras.t: Et super Dominum requiescebant, id est, divinæ auctoritati innitebantur; vel potius se inniti simulabant, quia ut eis a populo crederetur et copia rerum daretur, jactabant se ministros ac nuntios Dei. Vel, Super Dominum requiescebant, id est, de ejus bonitate præsumentes, dixerunt quietem, non impugnationem, esse futuram. Dicentes : Numquid non Dominus in medio nostrum? id est imo Deus vere in nobis est : quum tamen Salomon dicat, Longe est Dominus ab impiis. Non venient super nos mala pœnæ, id est, hostibus non trademur, nec capiemur, sed a Deo tanquam populus ejus protegemur.
paras.en: [[3:11|and they leaned upon the Lord|Et super Dominum requiescebant]], that is, they relied on God's authority; or rather they pretended to rely on it, since, so that the people might believe them and give them plenty of goods, they boasted that they were ministers and messengers of God. Or, [[3:11|they leaned upon the Lord|Super Dominum requiescebant]] [*requiescebant*, literally "they rested"], that is, presuming on his goodness, they said that there would be rest, not attack. [[3:11|saying: Is not the Lord in the midst of us?|Dicentes : Numquid non Dominus in medio nostrum?]] that is, nay, God is truly among us: whereas Solomon says: [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|Longe est Dominus ab impiis]]. [[3:11|no evil shall come among us|Non venient super nos mala]] (the evils of punishment), that is, we shall not be handed over to our enemies, nor taken, but shall be protected by God as his people.

paras.t: Propter hoc, id est propter præscripta peccata, Sion, id est illa pars Jerusalem in qua fuit templum atque palatium, quasi ager arabitur, id est, in solitudinem redigetur, ita ut possit arari, ædificiis destructis, habitatoribusque occisis; et Jerusalem quasi acervus lapidum erit, id est, penitus dejicetur; et mons templi, id est mons Sion, in quo steterat templum, erit et convertetur in excelsa silvarum, id est, fruteta et arbores altæ crescent in eo. Quæ omnia impleta sunt tempore Babylonicæ captivitatis, quæ septuaginta annis duravit. Quoniam tamen præmemorata facinora erant in populo Judæorum tempore Christi, quemadmodum Christus in Evangelio docet, redarguendo sacerdotes, Scribas ac Pharisæos de simulatione et hypocrisi, de superstitione et ambitione, præsertim de avaritia et pauperum devoratione ; ideo aliqui referunt ista ad primum Christi adventum, et captivitatem Judæorum a Romanis inflictam : præcipue, quoniam bona primitivæ Ecclesiæ diripientes principes sacerdotum ac judices, ædificabant Sion in sanguinibus, et in Jerusalem sanguinem Christi discipulorumque ejus fuderunt.
paras.en: [[3:12|Therefore|Propter hoc]], that is, because of the sins described above, [[3:12|Sion|Sion]], that is, that part of Jerusalem in which stood the temple and the palace, [[3:12|shall be ploughed as a field|quasi ager arabitur]], that is, shall be brought to a wilderness, so that it can be ploughed, its buildings destroyed and its inhabitants slain; [[3:12|and Jerusalem shall be as a heap of stones|et Jerusalem quasi acervus lapidum erit]], that is, shall be utterly thrown down; [[3:12|and the mountain of the temple|et mons templi]], that is, mount Sion, on which the temple had stood, shall be and shall be turned into [[3:12|the high places of the forests|in excelsa silvarum]], that is, thickets and tall trees shall grow on it. All of which was fulfilled at the time of the Babylonian captivity, which lasted seventy years. Since, however, the crimes recounted above were found in the Jewish people in the time of Christ, as Christ teaches in the Gospel, rebuking the priests, Scribes and Pharisees for pretence and hypocrisy, for superstition and ambition, and above all for avarice and devouring the poor, some therefore refer these words to the first coming of Christ and the captivity inflicted on the Jews by the Romans: chiefly because the chief priests and judges, plundering the goods of the primitive Church[[Heb 10:34||]], did [[3:10|build up Sion with blood|ædificabant Sion in sanguinibus]], and in Jerusalem shed the blood of Christ and of his disciples.

paras.t: Denique hujus prophetiæ atque Michææ istius mentionem efficit Jeremias. Quum enim sacerdotes et fallaces vellent Jeremiam occidere, quia Jerusalem dixit jam capiendam, surrexerunt quidam de senioribus, et dixerunt ad omnem cœtum populi : Michæas de Morasthi fuit propheta in diebus Ezechiæ regis Juda, et ait ad omnem populum : Hæc dicit Dominus : Sion quasi ager arabitur, et Jerusalem in acervum lapidum erit, et mons domus Domini in excelsa silvarum. Numquid morte condemnavit eum Ezechias et omnis Juda? Numquid non timuerunt et deprecati sunt Dominum, et pœnituit eum mali quod locutus fuerat contra eos? Hæc verba tam prolixe nunc allegavi, quia secundum allegantes hæc verba, præfatos videlicet seniores quorum allegationem Jeremias confirmare videtur, prophetia Michææ de destructione Jerusalem dicta fuit ad litteram pro tempore Ezechiæ, tanquam tunc adimplenda. Et secundum hoc, fuisset prophetia comminationis; postea tamen impleta fuit, ut dictum est.
paras.en: Lastly, Jeremias makes mention of this prophecy and of this Micheas. For when the priests and the deceivers wanted to kill Jeremias because he said that Jerusalem was soon to be taken, certain of the elders rose up, and [[Jer 26:17|they spoke to all the assembly of the people|dixerunt ad omnem cœtum populi]]: [[Jer 26:18|Micheas of Morasthi was a prophet in the days of Ezechias king of Juda|Michæas de Morasthi fuit propheta in diebus Ezechiæ regis Juda]], [[Jer 26:18|and he spoke to all the people|et ait ad omnem populum]]: [[Jer 26:18|Thus saith the Lord|Hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[Jer 26:18|Sion shall be ploughed like a field, and Jerusalem shall be a heap of stones|Sion quasi ager arabitur, et Jerusalem in acervum lapidum erit]], [[Jer 26:18|and the mountain of the house|et mons domus]] of the Lord [[Jer 26:18|the high places of woods|in excelsa silvarum]]. [[Jer 26:19|Did Ezechias king of Juda, and all Juda, condemn him to death?|Numquid morte condemnavit eum Ezechias et omnis Juda?]] [[Jer 26:19|did they not fear the Lord, and beseech the face of the Lord|Numquid non timuerunt et deprecati sunt Dominum]], [[Jer 26:19|and the Lord repented of the evil that he had spoken against them?|et pœnituit eum mali quod locutus fuerat contra eos?]] I have now cited these words at such length because, according to those who cited them, namely the elders mentioned, whose citation Jeremias seems to confirm, the prophecy of Micheas about the destruction of Jerusalem was spoken, in the letter, of the time of Ezechias, as to be fulfilled then. And on this view it would have been a prophecy of threatening [that is, a prophecy of what will happen unless men repent, as distinct from a prophecy of what God has fixed]; yet it was fulfilled afterwards, as has been said.

paras.t: INSUPER, secundum tropologicum intellectum, prælatis, sacerdotibus, doctoribus atque principibus Ecclesiæ dicitur : Audite, principes domus Jacob, id est Christianorum, qui sunt templum et domus Dei (de qua dicit Apostolus Timotheo : Scias quomodo oporteat te conversari in domo Dei), et judices domus Israel, id est militantis Ecclesiæ, Deum fide conspicientis. Qui abominamini judicium, et omnia recta pervertitis. Hoc non omnibus, sed indignis atque nocentibus competit : qui in judicando sequuntur amorem et odium, non rationem et æquitatem; nec dignantur redargui, sed dicunt implicite illud Sapientiæ, Sit autem fortitudo nostra lex justitiæ.
paras.en: Further, according to the tropological sense [that is, the moral sense], it is said to the prelates, priests, doctors and princes of the Church: [[3:9|Hear this, ye princes of the house of Jacob|Audite, principes domus Jacob]], that is, of Christians, who are the temple and house of God (of which the Apostle says to Timothy: [[1 Tim 3:15|that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God|Scias quomodo oporteat te conversari in domo Dei]]), [[3:9|and ye judges of the house of Israel|et judices domus Israel]], that is, of the Church militant, which beholds God by faith [*Israel* being taken as "seeing God"]. [[3:9|you that abhor judgment and pervert all that is right|Qui abominamini judicium, et omnia recta pervertitis]]. This fits not all, but the unworthy and harmful: who in judging follow love and hatred, not reason and equity; and who do not deign to be rebuked, but implicitly say that saying of Wisdom: [[Wis 2:11|But let our strength be the law of justice|Sit autem fortitudo nostra lex justitiæ]] [the words of the wicked in Wisdom: let our might be our rule of right].

paras.t: Qui ædificatis Sion, id est Ecclesiam, in sanguinibus, sacras Scripturas depravando, in cathedra pestilentiæ residendo, indignos ordinando, pusillos scandalizando ; et de eleemosynis pauperum, de patrimonio Christi pretiosas structuras levando. Et hoc est ædificare Jerusalem in peccatis.
paras.en: [[3:10|You that build up Sion|Qui ædificatis Sion]], that is, the Church, [[3:10|with blood|in sanguinibus]]: by corrupting the sacred Scriptures, by sitting [[Ps 1:1|in the chair of pestilence|in cathedra pestilentiæ]], by ordaining the unworthy, by scandalizing the little ones, and by raising costly buildings out of the alms of the poor, out of the patrimony of Christ. And this is to build Jerusalem in sins.

paras.t: Postremo, quomodo principes in muneribus judicent, sacerdotes quoque in mercede doceant, et fallaces quidam ac superstitiosi divinent, non est meæ parvitatis describere, quum (proh dolor!) ista nunc ad oculum pateant : dum omnes quæ sua sunt quæruntur, et temporalia spiritualibus præferunt; et hi qui alios ad salutarem timorem inducere obligantur, se ipsos ac alios vana promissione et periculosissima securitate decipiunt, dicentes : Numquid non Dominus in medio nostrum? Non venient super nos mala.
paras.en: Lastly, how princes judge [[3:11|for bribes|in muneribus]], priests too teach [[3:11|for hire|in mercede]], and certain deceivers and superstitious men divine, it is not for my littleness to describe, since (alas!) these things now lie open to the eye: while [[Phil 2:21|all seek the things that are their own|omnes quæ sua sunt quæruntur]], and prefer temporal things to spiritual; and those who are bound to lead others to a wholesome fear deceive themselves and others by vain promise and most perilous security, [[3:11|saying: Is not the Lord in the midst of us?|dicentes : Numquid non Dominus in medio nostrum?]] [[3:11|no evil shall come among us|Non venient super nos mala]].

paras.t: Propter hoc Sion quasi ager aratur, quia status Ecclesiæ hinc decrescit, et corda fidelium a dæmonibus arantur, ac pessimo semine seminantur. Jerusalem quoque quasi acervus lapidum est, dum caritate frigescente, dura atque lapidea fiunt fidelium corda. Et mons templi vertitur in excelsa silvarum, dum virtuosi et contemplativi labuntur, in superbiam eriguntur, et mundi dignitatibus atque opibus gaudent. Quod præcipue referri potest ad quosdam specie tenus religiosos, regulam suam non observantes, et ad sæcularia adspirantes.
paras.en: [[3:12|Therefore|Propter hoc]] [[3:12|Sion|Sion]] is ploughed [[3:12|as a field|quasi ager]], because the state of the Church is thereby in decline, and the hearts of the faithful are ploughed by demons and sown with the worst of seed. [[3:12|Jerusalem|Jerusalem]] also is [[3:12|as a heap of stones|quasi acervus lapidum]], while, as charity grows cold, the hearts of the faithful become hard and stony. [[3:12|and the mountain of the temple|Et mons templi]] is turned into [[3:12|the high places of the forests|in excelsa silvarum]], while the virtuous and contemplative fall away, are lifted up in pride, and take delight in the world's honours and riches. This may be referred especially to certain men who are religious in appearance only, who do not keep their rule and aspire to worldly things.

paras.t: Dicit autem Glossa circa hunc locum : Non debent ministri Ecclesiæ officia sua administrare propter pecuniam : non tamen prohibentur, quod ex officio debetur, accipere ad necessitatem, non ad luxuriam.
paras.en: Now the Gloss says on this place: The ministers of the Church ought not to discharge their offices for money; yet they are not forbidden to take what is due by reason of their office, for necessity, not for luxury.
